definitions.gloss: Dear Sir/Madam, To Whom It May Concern
definitions.explanation: A formal salutation used at the beginning of a Japanese letter. It is always paired with the closing salutation 敬具 (けいぐ, "Yours sincerely") at the end of the letter.

examples.japanese: {拝啓|はいけい}　{時下|じか}ますますご{清祥|せいしょう}のこととお{慶|よろこ}び{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: Dear Sir/Madam, I trust you are doing well.
examples.notes: A standard formal letter opening combining {拝啓|はいけい} with a seasonal greeting.

examples.japanese: {拝啓|はいけい}　{初春|しょしゅん}の{候|こう}、{皆様|みなさま}にはお{変|か}わりなくお{過|す}ごしのことと{存|ぞん}じます。
examples.english: Dear Sir/Madam, as the new year begins, I hope everyone is doing well.
examples.notes: An example with a seasonal reference ({時候|じこう}の{挨拶|あいさつ}).

examples.japanese: {手紙|てがみ}の{書|か}き{出|だ}しは「{拝啓|はいけい}」で{始|はじ}め、「{敬具|けいぐ}」で{結|むす}ぶのが{正式|せいしき}なマナーだ。
examples.english: Proper etiquette is to begin a letter with "haikei" and close it with "keigu."

notes:
{拝啓|はいけい} literally means "humbly stating" ({拝|はい} = humbly + {啓|けい} = to state/inform). It is the standard formal opening for Japanese letters and must always be paired with the closing {敬具|けいぐ} ("respectfully concluded").

FORMAT: In a Japanese letter, {拝啓|はいけい} is followed by a space (full-width) and then a seasonal greeting ({時候|じこう}の{挨拶|あいさつ}). The body of the letter follows, and the letter ends with {敬具|けいぐ}.

OTHER LETTER OPENINGS:
- {謹啓|きんけい}: more formal than {拝啓|はいけい} (paired with {謹白|きんぱく} or {敬白|けいはく})
- {前略|ぜんりゃく}: "dispensing with formalities" — used when skipping the seasonal greeting (paired with {草々|そうそう})

NOTE: {拝啓|はいけい} is used in formal business letters, official correspondence, and ceremonial writing. It is not used in casual emails or messages.
